At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
   

  

 Your role will be instrumental in designing the next generation of Affirm’s Checkout Platform to provide a world\-class buying experience that puts customers first!
   

  

 We are seeking a Backend Software Engineer to build out financial products and features providing new levels of accessibility and flexibility to our users.  Come join us as we build a beloved, lasting financial services brand predicated on honesty and trust. It’s going to be an amazing ride!

* Work with technical leaders in the team to design and implement insightful forward\-looking approaches that go beyond the direct team and solve large open\-ended problems
* Actively own components of checkout systems and define their long\-term health, while also improving the health of surrounding systems
* Collaborate with engineers within our team and across the organization to build the next generation of the checkout platform
* Learn and improve engineering standards, tooling, and processes across the checkout platform

* Take Ownership. You enjoy working with product and engineering leaders to develop detailed project definitions, and drive technical decisions within your team
* Execute. You have a proven track record of developing, testing, and shipping high\-quality software at scale
* Collaborate. You communicate clearly both verbally and in writing. If anything, you trend towards over\-communication
* Build Teams. You grow with engineers around you through sharing your learnings and providing feedback to your peers that will help the team grow
* Customer\-centric mentality. You are empathetic to the user experience and thoughtful about what we can do to make it better
* This position requires either equivalent practical experience or a Bachelor’s degree in a related field

* Python
* Kotlin
* RPC
* Redis
* MySQL
* AWS
* Github

Backend Engineers: Let 250\+ Companies Compete For You
 



  





 Fonzi is an AI recruiting company.
 



  





 No job boards. No recruiter spam. Companies request to interview you and submit salary bids upfront.
 



  





 Every week, hiring managers at 250\+ pre\-vetted startups in NYC and San Francisco review a curated group of engineers. They're reading profiles optimized by our team to surface what matters: what you've built, how you think about systems, and whether you're the kind of engineer who ships.
 



  





 Companies on Fonzi are Applied AI startups, Frontier labs, Hypergrowth startups, PE firms starting lean AI teams and more. They're backed by investors like A16z, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Y Combinator and more.
 



  





 How It Works
 


* 5\-minute application
* We reach out, learn what you're building and what excites you, and optimize your profile
* Hiring managers review the cohort and request interviews with candidates they want
* Companies submit competing salary bids directly to you
* You only interview where you're genuinely interested
* Completely free. We have an iMessage agent \+ humans in the loop you can text anytime w/ questions or requests to help handle scheduling and coordination



  





 Who We're Looking For
 



  





 The backend engineers who do best on Fonzi:
 


* Have built and scaled backend systems in production: APIs, services, databases and queues
* Are strong in Python, Go, TypeScript, Java or Rust, and deep in Postgres or similar
* Think in data models, distributed systems and failure modes
* Have built backends for LLM\-powered products (orchestration, tool calling, retrieval, async jobs) or want to
* Thrive in startup environments where the problem is ambiguous and the team is small
* Have 2\-8 years of experience, ideally with experience at at least one high\-growth company



  





 What You'll Build
 



  





 The companies on Fonzi are working on:
 


* Backends powering agentic workflows across healthcare, fintech, legal and logistics
* High\-throughput APIs and integrations with complex enterprise systems
* Payments, trading and real\-time financial infrastructure
* Event\-driven architectures and data pipelines that scale with the business
* LLM orchestration layers: tool calling, retrieval, job queues and eval hooks



  





 Compensation
 


* $175,000 to $290,000\+ base salary depending on experience and role. Many positions include meaningful equity at pre\-seed through Series B stage companies.



  





 The Interview Process (Typical)
 


* Screening conversation looking for communication skills, cultural fit and genuine curiosity about AI
* Technical deep\-dive on system design: APIs, data models and scaling
* Coding or pairing session on a realistic backend problem



  





 If you care about building systems that don't break when the product takes off, we want to hear from you.

Join Cleveland Clinic’s Main Campus where research and surgery are advanced, technology is leading\-edge, patient care is world class and caregivers are family. Here, you will work alongside a passionate and dedicated team, receive endless support and appreciation, and build a rewarding career with one of the most respected healthcare organizations in the world.
   

  

 The H60 Neurosciences Nursing Unit cares for complex neurological medical and surgical patients diagnosed with conditions such as stroke, Multiple Sclerosis, brain and spine tumors, Parkinson’s Disease, Epilepsy, Guillain\-Barre Syndrome, Myasthenia Gravis, degenerative brain diseases and spinal disorders. Located on Main Campus, the H60 unit is certified as part of a Comprehensive Stroke Center within Cleveland Clinic’s nationally ranked Neurological Institute and our nursing caregiver staff members are highly trained specialists in advanced neurological assessment techniques.
   

  

 Our unit prides itself on providing new caregiver orientation that is individualized to ensure success. We encourage participation in opportunities to enhance the orientation learning experience such as operating room observation time, interactive case studies with our nurse practitioners and residents, clinic observations and more. We also support new nurses with one\-on\-one preceptors, as well as weekly progress meetings.
   

  

 Join our unit and take part in some of the most complex procedures in healthcare, such as craniotomies for brain tumors, shunts, aneurysm coiling/clipping, deep brain stimulators, SA drain evaluations, spinal procedures, laminectomy, discectomy and fusions with hardware.

 Access Medical Laboratories is seeking an innovative and business\-focused Data Scientist to join our Digital Transformation team. Reporting to the Digital Transformation Manager, this role will leverage artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), predictive analytics, and data science techniques to develop solutions that improve operational efficiency, customer experience, and business performance across Operations, Finance, Commercial/Marketing, and Laboratory functions.

* Develop and implement AI and machine learning solutions that improve operational efficiency and business outcomes across multiple departments.
* Collaborate with business leaders to identify opportunities where AI and advanced analytics can solve operational challenges.

* Design, develop, validate, and deploy production\-ready AI/ML models.
* Monitor model performance and continuously optimize solutions based on business outcomes.
* Analyze large, complex datasets to identify trends, patterns, and opportunities for improvement.
* Build dashboards and reporting tools that communicate insights to technical and non\-technical stakeholders.
* Partner with IT, software development, laboratory operations, finance, and commercial teams to integrate AI solutions into existing workflows.
* Ensure data quality, governance, and compliance with healthcare data standards and organizational policies.
* Stay current on emerging AI technologies and recommend innovative applications that drive competitive advantage.

**Why Transmission Line Engineering?**
 The U.S. power grid is one of the most stable and in\-demand fields in engineering, and it's only growing. Much of the country's transmission infrastructure is decades old and due for replacement. At the same time, electricity demand is rising fast, driven by data centers, AI, and electrification. Utilities need engineers who can design the lines that make that growth possible, and that need isn't going away.
   

  

 Transmission line engineering is a unique, specialized niche within civil engineering, and it tends to pay well compared with many other civil disciplines. You'll also pick up a working knowledge of electrical engineering, and you may be surprised how familiar it feels. Electricity flowing through a line behaves a lot like water flowing through a pipe, so the hydraulics and fluids concepts you learned in school carry over.
   

  

**Responsibilities**
* Design and analyze transmission line systems, including structures, conductors, and foundations.
* Prepare detailed engineering drawings, material lists, calculations, specifications, and reports.
* Conduct site visits and inspections to ensure compliance with design standards and safety regulations.
* Collaborate with utility clients, project managers, contractors, and other engineers to ensure successful project execution in Nevada and across the U.S.
* Utilize advanced software tools for modeling and simulation of transmission line performance (PLS\-CADD and PLS\-POLE – we'll train you).
* Stay up to date with industry trends, standards, and best practices.


**Minimum Qualifications**
* Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering (completed, or expected by May 2027\).
* EIT or plans to pass the FE exam within the first year
* Comfortable working outdoors and traveling to project sites
* Valid driver's license


**Preferred Qualifications**
* Structural or geotechnical coursework
* Internship or co\-op experience in civil, structural, or utility work
* Any exposure to transmission line design and analysis software (e.g., PLS\-CADD, PLS\-POLE).

**ABOUT THE POSITION** 




  





 Groundswell builds community power \- cutting electricity bills for the neighbors who need savings most through community solar, resilience hubs, and home energy efficiency and repair. Gratava is the AI\-enabled data platform underneath that work: a neutral coordination layer where a household proves eligibility once and that verified record unlocks every program they qualify for.
 



  





 Forward deployed means living with our users, customers, and partners. The Forward Deployed Engineer will sit with utility staff, program administrators, caseworkers and households to find what blocks or limits adoption and success \- then build the prototypes that prove the solution works, validate it with the customer, and hand it off to production engineering. Customer contact and building are one job here.
 



  





 Reporting to the SVP, Data Platform, the Forward Deployed Engineer is a peer to the Tech Lead with distinct ownership: the Forward Deployed Engineer proves what should be built, and the Tech Lead is responsible for what ships in production. You will write production\-quality code, and what you build is judged by whether it proves the answer rather than by whether it ships \- deployment into production, and the policies and controls that go with it, stay with the Tech Lead.
 



  





**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES** 




 •
 **Field discovery** 
 . Work directly with our internal teams and with utilities, program administrators, agencies and households to understand where systems, policies, and data break down in practice. You will investigate hard problems such as premise resolution, income verification, eligibility determination, program matching, and other rules that have not yet been defined.
 



 •
 **Build the proof.** 
 Turn ambiguous problems into working software. Build new core functionality at the prototype level \- the matching engine, the rules\-as\-logic layer, the AI agent layer \- connected to real data sources and run against real records. Be responsible for both demonstrating an idea and building enough of it to prove whether it works and adds value. Prototype here means scope, not craft \- you write code good enough to run in production, even though production deployment is determined by the Tech Lead.
 



 •
 **Program rules into working logic** 
 . Translate complex heterogeneous program
 



 requirements into reliable, testable logic such as income thresholds, categorical
 



 eligibility, funding stack sequencing, pre\-weatherization gating and other program
 



 specific conditions in ways that are explainable, auditable, and resilient.
 



 •
 **Validate with the customer.** 
 Responsible for building prototypes and testing with
 



 the people who will use them. Before production engineering begins, establish
 



 three things: the data sources work as expected; the logic produces the correct
 



 outcomes, and the interface is simple enough for customers to understand and
 



 use.
 



 •
 **Create a clean path to production** 
 . Deliver a working proof, the data connections,
 



 technical decisions behind it, and a clear specification that distinguishes what is
 



 essential from what is not. Give production engineering enough clarity to complete
 



 the work without having to discover the problem.
 



 •
 **Scope the roadmap** 
 . Turn technical discovery into actionable products and
 



 engineering decisions. Provide fast, reliable feasibility assessments and effort
 



 estimates that leadership and engineering can use to make and commit to
 



 roadmap decisions.
 



 •
 **Continual Development and Growth** 
 . Share what you know and learn with the
 



 broader engineering team. Partner closely with the Tech Lead to transfer agentic
 



 tooling practice and document knowledge that compounds across the team.
 



  





**ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES** 




 As a member of the Groundswell team, the Forward Deployed Engineer is expected to
 



 participate in the overall execution of Groundswell programs, including support for
 



 program launches, partner engagements, and organization\-wide initiatives as needs
 



 arise.
 



  





**OTHER DUTIES** 




 This position description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of
 



 activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required. Duties, obligations, and activities
 



 may change at any time with or without notice.
 



  





**COMPETENCIES OR SPECIALIZED KNOWLEDGE** 




 • Writes production\-ready code \- able to work to production standards, and able to
 



 judge when a proof is good enough to stop.
 



 • Comfortable in the field with customers \- builds fast, validates directly, and hands
 



 off cleanly.
 



 • Judgment about scope \- knows what not to build while a customer is pushing, and
 



 can defend it to a non\-technical stakeholder.
 



 • Comfort in regulated environments: consent, audit logging, role\-based access, and
 



 data governance.
 



 • Able to work independently in an early\-stage environment with limited scaffolding
 



 and shifting priorities.
 



  





**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY**

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

 month in alignment with Groundswell’s hybrid/remote work plan.
 



  





**POSITION TYPE AND EXPECTED HOURS** 




 This is a full\-time, 40\-hour\-a\-week position. The days and hours of work are Monday
 



 through Friday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, and core hours are from 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
 



 Occasional evening and weekend work may be required as job duties demand.
 



  





**TRAVEL**

 new deployments. Occasional visits to Groundswell office locations may also be required.
 



  





**REQUIRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

 equivalent practical experience. We weight demonstrated work over credentials.

 into working logic.

 agentic development tools as normal practice.

 program experience.

**POSITION SUMMARY** 




 We are seeking a Data Science Analyst to support end\-to\-end data science delivery by translating business questions into analyses, model components, and production\-ready outputs under guidance across our cruise line client. This role emphasizes Data Science ownership of delivered business value: framing the right problem, building and validating ML/optimization/GenAI solutions, partnering on deployment, monitoring performance, and driving adoption in production. The ideal candidate combines statistical and machine learning depth with practical business judgment, strong stakeholder partnership, and the ability to convert analytical work into measurable outcomes rather than isolated prototypes.
 



  





**ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES** 



* **Problem Framing \& Value:** 
 Frame high\-impact business problems for entry\-level analytics and supervised model delivery into measurable data science opportunities with clear decision owners, baseline metrics, adoption paths, and expected value tied to decision support, operational visibility, and early\-stage automation.
* **Predictive Modeling:** 
 Develop forecasting, propensity, classification, and ranking models using Python, scikit\-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and Databricks feature workflows to support production decisions.
* **Prescriptive Decisioning:** 
 Build recommendation, simulation, and optimization solutions using MILP, heuristics, dynamic programming, or scenario modeling to improve operational and commercial decisions.
* **GenAI Solutions:** 
 Design GenAI workflows using GPT\-class models, Azure AI Foundry, RAG, embeddings, prompt engineering, and evaluation routines where natural\-language or agentic capabilities improve business productivity.
* **Statistical Experimentation:** 
 Design and evaluate A/B tests, quasi\-experiments, causal analyses, bootstrap methods, and non\-parametric tests to determine whether model or process changes create measurable lift.
* **Explainability \& Trust:** 
 Apply SHAP, sensitivity analysis, model diagnostics, error analysis, and stakeholder\-ready explanations so users understand model behavior, limits, and decision implications.
* **Production Deployment:** 
 Partner with AI Engineering to deploy models and analytical applications through Databricks, Azure ML, MLflow, APIs, or containerized services while retaining accountability for business value and model behavior.
* **Production Operations:** 
 Monitor accuracy, drift, bias, adoption, latency, cost, and business KPIs; trigger retraining, recalibration, or process changes when performance or value realization degrades.
* **Stakeholder Partnership:** 
 Partner with business, product, operations, AI Engineering, and data engineering teams to convert model outputs into decisions, workflows, incentives, and measurable adoption.



  





**QUALIFICATIONS / KNOWLEDGE / SKILLS** 



* **Education:** 
 Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Operations Research, Engineering, Economics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
* **Experience:** 
 Demonstrated experience appropriate to entry scope delivering ML, optimization, experimentation, or GenAI solutions that moved beyond analysis into production use or business decisioning.
* **ML Tooling:** 
 Hands\-on experience with Python, scikit\-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, PyTorch or TensorFlow where appropriate, and model evaluation workflows for production\-grade use cases.
* **Optimization:** 
 Experience with MILP solvers, simulation, scenario planning, dynamic programming, heuristics, or prescriptive analytics methods applied to real business decisions.
* **GenAI Platforms:** 
 Experience with Azure AI Foundry, GPT\-class models, RAG, embeddings, prompt engineering, evaluation, and safe use of GenAI for decision support or workflow automation.
* **Data Platforms:** 
 Advanced use of Databricks, Spark, SQL, feature pipelines, data quality checks, and reproducible analytical workflows for large\-scale data science delivery.
* **MLOps:** 
 Experience with MLflow, Azure ML, model registries, CI/CD, monitoring, retraining, and production handoff practices that keep models reliable after launch.
* **Engineering:** 
 Strong Python engineering practices, Git workflows, testing, packaging, notebooks\-to\-production discipline, APIs, and collaboration with AI Engineering for deployment readiness.
* **Communication:** 
 Clear communication skills with data scientists, product owners, analysts, and business stakeholders, including the ability to explain model logic, uncertainty, tradeoffs, risks, and recommended decisions in business terms.

**About Alex \& The Role**
 Alex is an AI recruiter. Alex screens and interviews candidates over voice — on the web and over the phone — and it works inside the systems companies already recruit with: their applicant tracking system, their requisitions, their hiring process. Enterprises and staffing firms use it to run interviews at a volume they otherwise couldn't.
   

  

 Forward\-Deployed Engineers are the technical owners of every Alex deployment. When a customer signs, FDEs are the people who make Alex work inside their systems and their process — and keep it working. It is the most end\-to\-end engineering role at the company: you design the solution, build it, integrate it, ship it to production, and own it afterwards.
   

  

 What you'll do
   

  

* Design and build how a customer uses Alex. Turn a hiring process described in a meeting into workflows that actually run — triggers, filters, interview guides, and the actions we take back in their ATS. When a customer needs something their setup doesn't do yet, you drive it: design, build, test, roll out, verify.
* Own the integration surface. We integrate with roughly two dozen applicant tracking systems, some directly and some through a unified API partner. You'll build new integrations, maintain existing ones, and go deep on the ones you own — along with the other systems a customer's workflow reaches into, like assessment providers and identity verification.
* Run the technical side of onboarding. Connection, permissions and scopes, job import, field mapping, workflow build, test interviews, go\-live — sequenced so nothing is discovered in front of a candidate.
* Own the deployments in production. The team owns the support queue — for customers and candidates both — and diagnoses to root cause rather than working around it. You'll also build the monitoring that catches problems before a customer has to call.
* Be the technical voice of the customer. You are the person who sees, across many accounts, where the product runs out. Turning that into an evidenced case our product engineering team can act on is part of the job.


 What we're looking for
   

  

* Real engineering ability. This role reads code, writes code, and ships changes. It is not a technical\-adjacent role.
* Comfort working inside someone else's system with incomplete documentation. Much of this job is finding out what a third\-party API actually does, as opposed to what its docs claim.
* Debugging instinct — the reflex to go get the evidence rather than reason from the symptom.
* Direct customer contact without a buffer. You'll run your own working sessions and say hard things clearly.
* Strong writing. A large fraction of the output of this role is a clear written explanation.


 Nice to have
   

  

* Forward\-deployed, implementation, solutions, or integrations engineering experience — especially anywhere with a long tail of third\-party systems.
* You've built against a messy enterprise API and lived with the result.
* Fluency with observability tooling — logs, traces, dashboards, alerting you had to live with.


 If you've gotten this far and this role resonates with you, we want you to apply. Your first conversation will be with Alex, our AI recruiter.
